sources.RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria: docs/rfcs/2026-08-21-otp-external-devices.md, task OTP-23 acceptance criteria and verification evidence
sources.user directive 2026-10-26: revision request recorded in docs/otp-23-contract-alignment.md (strict background, attribute budget, macOS identity, plain runtime)
sources.user steering 2026-10-26: account waiver: tests requiring new accounts are non-blocking for OTP-23; recorded as an acceptance scope revision in the RFC

rows.requirement: Stable Chrome launches the plain host on demand from a STANDARD non-admin Windows account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Host starts via runtime.connectNative with no elevation; account token is not an administrator. (Historical runs used an administrator account at medium integrity.)
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: Host creates no window and communicates only through Chrome-owned stdin/stdout
rows.expected: Zero top-level windows and zero network endpoints owned by the host and its wrapper during connect, transfer and shutdown.

rows.requirement: Extension-owned search receives bounded device events
rows.expected: start_scan yields device_found events within the documented bounds; stop_scan ends them.

rows.requirement: Two phones independently exchange synthetic complete records (fresh build of this branch)
rows.expected: Byte-exact replies per original handle for both phones; distinct handles; MTU before CCCD.

rows.requirement: Attribute-budget boundaries at ATT MTU 517 with the revised contract
rows.expected: Byte-exact on both phones for 4, 177/178/179, 507/508/509, 1015/1016/1017, 4095/4096 bytes; no Android exception; fragments <= 512 bytes.

rows.requirement: Disconnect affects only its handle
rows.expected: Stale handle rejects sends; the surviving phone still exchanges a 4096-byte record.

rows.requirement: Chrome port closure stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: Host and wrapper gone after port.disconnect(); BLE links released.

rows.requirement: stdin EOF stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: Same cleanup after the extension stdin pipe closes without a shutdown request.

rows.requirement: shutdown stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: shutdown_complete is the last message; host gone.

rows.requirement: Unsupported or denied radio/permission states are classified
rows.expected: Bluetooth off, adapter absent and access-denied each return a classified error with the documented recoverability.

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, COLD idle (no prior exchange)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Connector hidden >= 10 min with another ordinary tab focused, NO DevTools client of any kind, no audio/WebRTC/keepalive; both phones' unsolicited 4096-byte records arrive byte-exact while hidden (scripts/strict_background.py --scenario cold).

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, PREWARMED link (separate run)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Same as W-11 after one byte-verified exchange per phone (--scenario prewarm). Reported separately; never combined with W-11.

rows.requirement: Unsigned development-registered host launches from Chrome in a FRESH STANDARD non-admin macOS account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Chrome starts the host; no administrator involvement; a disposable Chrome profile with its own Native Messaging manifest.
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: TCC Bluetooth prompt owner (Chrome vs host) in a FRESH account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Records which process the prompt/grant attaches to and whether a prompt fires for the headless child. (Historical: grant owner unknown; not formal attribution.)
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: Signed production-shaped host (stable bundle identity, usage descriptions, final identifier me.nagaev.veles.bridge) with signing provenance
rows.expected: Directly signed fixture with the final bundle identifier and recorded signing provenance; prompt owner observed on the existing account. NOT waived. (Historical Apple Development me.nagaev.veles.otp23.poc is not proof of the production identity.)
rows.blocker: Mac has Apple Development only: no Developer ID and no final-identifier fixture exists; needs the final identity/credentials plus a human-observed prompt on the existing account

rows.requirement: DENY result and exact System Settings retry guidance
rows.expected: Deny produces access_denied with exact System Settings guidance; the prompt owner (Chrome vs host) is recorded as observed on the existing account; no TCC reset used.
rows.blocker: requires a human to deny the prompt on the existing account (account type to be recorded truthfully as admin or standard)

rows.requirement: ALLOW result
rows.expected: Allow yields allowed_always and discovery works for the same binary.
rows.blocker: requires a human to allow the prompt on the existing account (account type to be recorded truthfully as admin or standard)

rows.requirement: Recovery after deny -> allowed_always with the SAME extension state, no reinstall
rows.expected: After granting in System Settings, search recovers without reinstalling and without losing extension state.
rows.blocker: requires a human grant on the existing account with the same Chrome profile/extension state across the transition (account type recorded truthfully)

rows.requirement: Two phones independently exchange synthetic complete records incl. attribute-budget boundaries (fresh build)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Byte-exact for the W-05 size list on both phones using the measured max write-without-response (512 -> attribute 512, payload 508; no invented MTU).

rows.requirement: No window; port closure, stdin EOF and shutdown each leave no process
rows.expected: As W-02, W-07, W-08, W-09 on macOS.

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, COLD idle
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: As W-11 on macOS.

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, PREWARMED link (separate run)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: As W-12 on macOS.

rows.requirement: Interop defects found by the physical runs are fixed or recorded (#120 M3 duplicate STATE_CONNECTED, M4 CCCD/MTU ordering)
rows.expected: Duplicate connected callback keeps a healthy link; MTU-before-CCCD observed on Windows and macOS clients; CCCD-before-MTU rejected with record I/O gated.

rows.requirement: #120 M6: two CENTRALS on ONE phone (independent 4096-byte downstream records, no cross-peer disconnect)
rows.expected: Explicitly different from two phones on one central; not discharged by W-04/M-07.

rows.requirement: Current Tauri-vs-plain dependency, SBOM and size evidence justifies (or not) retaining Tauri solely for OTP-25 packaging
rows.expected: A recorded current comparison (dependency graph, SBOM, binary size, packaging proof) that justifies the choice. Historical 1a34191 costs are kept separate and are not current evidence.
rows.blocker: dependency graphs measured today (evidence/current-dependency-cost.json) but current Windows/macOS binary sizes, SBOMs and a packaging proof need the coordinating agent's builds; no justification is asserted

rows.requirement: Explicit OTP-23 feasibility decision recorded after all rows are resolved
rows.expected: GO only when every row above is PASS, except NOT RUN rows carrying the user-approved account waiver (non-blocking, never PASS); otherwise NO-GO for OTP-24.
